title: Strict transform commutes with affine pushforward
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and let $b:S^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of $S$-schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $g_b:X\times_SS^b\to Y\times_SS^b$ for the base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $\mathcal F^b$ denotes the module strict transform relative to $\mathcal I$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform], then there is a canonical isomorphism $g_{b,*}\mathcal F^b\cong(g_*\mathcal F)^b$ of $\mathcal O_{Y\times_SS^b}$-modules.

proof.text: Put $X_b=X\times_SS^b$, $Y_b=Y\times_SS^b$, with projections $p_X:X_b\to X$, $p_Y:Y_b\to Y$, and $q_X:X_b\to S^b$, $q_Y:Y_b\to S^b$. The square with edges $g_b,p_X,g,p_Y$ is cartesian by the fibre-product universal property: its objects classify compatible maps to $X,Y,S^b$. Thus $g_b$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). Set $H_X=p_X^*\mathcal F$ and $H_Y=p_Y^*g_*\mathcal F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change](1), $g_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and the specified base-change map is an isomorphism $\beta:H_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{b,*}H_X$. Both $H_X$ and $H_Y$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-ringed-space-tensor-pullback-qcoh]. This applies to $g:X\to Y$ with base-change map $p_Y:Y_b\to Y$, with no flatness condition on $b$.

source.place: Tag 080G, first proof sentence; Morphisms 01SD and Cohomology of Schemes 02KG; quasi-coherent pullback is Modules 01BG.

proof.text: Write $E=b^{-1}V(\mathcal I)$ and $D_X=q_X^{-1}E$, $D_Y=q_Y^{-1}E$. Then $D_X=g_b^{-1}D_Y$. The extended centre on $S^b$ is locally generated by one element by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]; after pullback its vanishing set on $X_b$ is locally $V(a)$, with no nonzerodivisor assertion on $X_b$. Consequently the open inclusion $j_X:X_b\setminus D_X\hookrightarrow X_b$ is quasi-compact: for any affine open $W$, choose an affine cover of $W$ refining these neighbourhoods and take a finite subcover, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and quasi-compactness of affine spectra [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii). In each member the complement is $D(a)$, homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](ii), hence quasi-compact by the same spectrum lemma. A finite union of these is $W\setminus D_X$. The diagonal of an open inclusion is an isomorphism, so $j_X$ is also quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism].

source.place: Paragraph preceding Tag 080D and Tag 080G; the locally principal complement argument supplies the retrocompactness used in Properties 07ZP.

proof.text: Let $K_X\subseteq H_X$ be the subsheaf consisting of sections whose restriction outside $D_X$ is zero, as in [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. It is precisely $\ker(H_X\to j_{X,*}(H_X|_{X_b\setminus D_X}))$, since kernels of module sheaves are computed on sections [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Restriction of $H_X$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-ringed-space-tensor-pullback-qcoh]. The preceding step supplies the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses for [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh], so the target of this restriction map is quasi-coherent. The kernel lemma therefore makes $K_X$ quasi-coherent. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2) to $K_X\hookrightarrow H_X$ makes $Q_X=H_X/K_X$ quasi-coherent as well, and the strict-transform definition identifies $Q_X=\mathcal F^b$.

source.place: Properties Tag 07ZP, proof of lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset (kernel description); Tag 080D(1).

proof.text: Let $K_Y\subseteq H_Y$ consist of sections zero outside $D_Y$, the subsheaf defining $(g_*\mathcal F)^b$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Under $\beta$, it equals $g_{b,*}K_X$ as a submodule of $g_{b,*}H_X$. Indeed, on any open $U\subseteq Y_b$, a section of the latter sheaf is $s\in H_X(g_b^{-1}U)$. It belongs to $g_{b,*}K_X(U)$ exactly when $s|_{g_b^{-1}U\setminus D_X}=0$. Since $D_X=g_b^{-1}D_Y$, this is exactly vanishing on $g_b^{-1}(U\setminus D_Y)$, equivalently vanishing of the corresponding section of $H_Y$ on $U\setminus D_Y$. This uses only that the sheaf isomorphism $\beta$ commutes with restriction; it proves equality of the actual submodules, not an assertion about stalks of pushforward.

source.place: Tag 080G, middle proof sentences; Properties Tag 07ZQ, lemma-push-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, with its sectionwise verification written out.

proof.text: Consider $g_{b,*}(H_X\to Q_X)$. For every affine open $U\subseteq Y_b$, $W=g_b^{-1}U$ is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](3) to the inclusion $K_X\hookrightarrow H_X$ on the affine open $W$: the quotient map $H_X(W)\to Q_X(W)$ is surjective with kernel $K_X(W)$. These are exactly the sections over $U$ of the displayed pushed-forward map. Since affine opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], this map is an epimorphism of sheaves, and its sectionwise kernel on every open is $g_{b,*}K_X$. Thus it exhibits $g_{b,*}Q_X$ as the quotient $(g_{b,*}H_X)/(g_{b,*}K_X)$. This is the precise exactness of affine pushforward needed here; it is applied only to the quasi-coherent terms verified in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 080G, final proof sentence; Schemes Tags 01IB, 01IC and 01LB give the affine cokernel computation.

proof.text: The isomorphism $\beta^{-1}:g_{b,*}H_X\to H_Y$ takes the submodule $g_{b,*}K_X$ exactly onto $K_Y$ by Step 4. It therefore induces an isomorphism on their quotients: the inverse is induced by $\beta$, and the two composites are the identity because this is true before taking the quotient. Using Step 5 and the two quotient definitions [def-trf-module-strict-transform] gives $g_{b,*}\mathcal F^b\cong H_Y/K_Y=(g_*\mathcal F)^b$. The induced map is characterized by composing with the quotient map from $g_{b,*}H_X$; all choices in the local verification disappear from this characterization. Hence this is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y_b}$-modules.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q31-5f90594d7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, all six steps, and the statement of every cited node. Sources read: Stacks divisors.tex 080G (lemma-strict-transform-affine, statement and proof), 080D (definition-strict-transform) and the retrocompactness paragraph before it, and properties.tex 07ZP (the proof of (3) through the kernel of F -> j_*F|) and 07ZQ. The statement is unchanged. It matches 080G except for the finite-type centre restriction, which the parent fixed when it created the node and which the module strict-transform definition needs; this is not a target, so nothing is weakened. Step 1: X_b is identified with X x_Y Y_b. Affineness comes from permanence (1), and the 02KG base-change map along p_Y comes from affine-pushforward-base-change (1). Step 2: D_X = g_b^{-1}D_Y. The exceptional ideal is locally principal by principalization, using the same finite-type centre. j_X is quasi-compact by refining to affines, taking a finite subcover and using D(a) = Spec A_a, and quasi-separated because it is an open immersion; this is elementary from the cited statements. Step 3: K_X is the kernel of restriction, as in 07ZP; its target is quasi-coherent by the qcqs-pushforward node, and the kernel and cokernel nodes make K_X and the quotient quasi-coherent. Step 4: an elementary sectionwise proof that K_Y matches g_{b,*}K_X under beta; it does not need the qcqs hypothesis of 07ZQ. Step 5: the affine cokernel formula (clause 3) holds on the affine preimages; surjectivity on a basis gives an epimorphism, and its kernel is g_{b,*}K_X because two subsheaves equal on a basis are equal. Clause (1) of the same cited node would also give this, so the missing clause pointer is not a fault. Step 6: the induced isomorphism of quotients is correct. Small cases tested: g = id, F = 0, unit ideal, zero ideal, the blowup of the plane at the origin with X = V(x) as a closed affine subscheme (both sides give the pushforward of the strict-transform line), and an exceptional generator that becomes a zero divisor after pullback. There are no new nodes, and no DAG node duplicates the item. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and every citation in a step's text is in its uses. No SGA is cited. I accept the six declared tool_uses as generic black boxes. No fixes were made.
